themes_detail.label: Park Noise Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Park noise complaints exploded to 4 this week versus a baseline of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks — a 3100% spike (z-score: 11.72) — suggesting a new or intensifying noise source at a community amenity during a season when outdoor use peaks.
evidence: 4 park noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 11.72)
Highest statistical anomaly in dataset by z-score, indicating unprecedented deviation
Timing aligns with warmer months when parks see peak usage
reporting_angles: Which park is generating complaints and what is the noise source (events, construction, groups)?
Are Parks Dept. enforcement resources adequate to respond to emerging complaints?

themes_detail.label: Curb and Street Sign Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition and damaged street sign complaints both spiked to 4 this week—each representing 357% increases from the 8-week baseline (0.9 complaints/week)—suggesting accelerating street infrastructure decay across the district.
evidence: 4 curb condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly average (357% spike, z-score: 4.0)
4 street sign damage complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly average (357% spike, z-score: 4.0)
Simultaneous spike in two infrastructure categories suggests systematic neglect or recent weather/traffic damage
reporting_angles: Are curbs and street signs failing at the same locations or distributed across district?
What is DOT's current maintenance cycle and backlog in CD 305?

themes_detail.label: Underground Infrastructure Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Root, sewer, and sidewalk condition complaints reached 13 last week—a 215% spike from the 4.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 6.51)—while plumbing complaints hit 6 last week versus 1.2 average (380% spike, z-score: 3.96), indicating widespread subsurface and drainage failures.
evidence: 13 root/sewer/sidewalk complaints LAST WEEK vs. 4.1 weekly average (215% spike, z-score: 6.51)
6 plumbing complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly average (380% spike, z-score: 3.96)
Converges with long-standing CB budget request for street infrastructure; 507 DOB permits filed in last 90 days suggest construction activity may be exacerbating underground issues
reporting_angles: Are recent construction projects (118 new building permits, 323 alterations in 90 days) damaging sewer and water lines?
Which blocks are hotspots for root infiltration and sewer backup?
What is DEP's response timeline to widespread complaints?

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Wave
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints peaked at 38 three weeks ago—a 744% jump from the 4.5 weekly baseline (z-score: 6.95)—though this spike is now aging out of the "this week" window, it represents a recent district-wide tagging or vandalism surge worth investigating for ongoing activity.
evidence: 38 graffiti complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 4.5 weekly average (744% spike, z-score: 6.95)
Second-highest z-score in dataset after park noise; indicates major but time-shifted event
No follow-up data to confirm whether spike has subsided or persists
reporting_angles: Was the spike concentrated on specific corridors or buildings, or district-wide?
Has graffiti activity resumed at baseline levels, or is it ongoing at elevated rates?
Are crews or gang activity responsible, and what is NYPD's enforcement response?

themes_detail.label: Dead and Dying Trees
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints hit 3 last week—a 1100% spike from the 0.2 weekly baseline (z-score: 6.35)—signaling potential disease, pest, or environmental stress affecting street tree canopy during spring season.
evidence: 3 dead/dying tree complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score: 6.35)
Aligns with Parks CB budget request to 'improve access to a park or amenity' and address canopy health
Spring season timing suggests seasonal disease (emerald ash borer, anthracnose) or winter damage assessment
reporting_angles: Is a specific pest or disease affecting trees (e.g., emerald ash borer in ash trees)?
Which streets or parks have the highest concentration of dying trees?
What is Parks Dept. removal and replanting capacity in CD 305?
